prize_parts.citation: For the development of dye-sensitized nanocrystalline solar cells, in which molecular dyes on mesoporous oxide films convert light to electricity.
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage.

statement.case_for: I now propose two parts. B025: the 1991 O'Regan and Grätzel cell is a designed architecture, a mesoporous nanocrystalline oxide carrying a molecular sensitizer and a redox mediator, whose structure sets its function. It founded molecular photovoltaics, supplied the dyes, electrolytes and interface concepts that later work relied on, and has more than thirty years of independent confirmation and some commercial use. The attribution to two names follows the origin paper and the sustained development program. B024: I moved here because the round-1 exchange answered my main objection. The adenine base editor required evolving TadA, an RNA-acting enzyme, to deaminate DNA adenine, which no natural enzyme does. That is new chemistry from design and evolution, not just a Cas9 fusion, and it is independently reproduced and in patients. I accept Liu as the central originator, and the cap leaves room for one more seat only if the citation is kept narrow. The pairing is two enabling capabilities, one in materials and one in genome chemistry, each explainable in a sentence and each tied to a specific structural or mechanistic step.
statement.case_against: Against B025: dye-sensitized cells did not reach the efficiency or cost once promised and were displaced by perovskites and silicon, so a prize may look backward, and Hagfeldt's later contributions go uncredited under a two-name cut. Against B024: it follows the 2020 CRISPR prize closely, and Liu alone excludes Komor and Gaudelli, whose first-author papers are decisive, and leaves the Kondo and Nishida priority question open. Against the pairing: the two parts share no theme beyond enabling design, so it risks looking like two single-achievement prizes stapled together, and a colleague who prefers the B024 plus B009 pairing has a more thematically coherent case than mine.

responses.point: Adenine base editing is the strongest evidence of real chemistry, because no natural DNA adenine deaminase existed and TadA had to be evolved to act on DNA.
responses.response: This is the argument that moved me. In round 1 I treated base editing as largely protein engineering on the 2020 platform. The need to evolve a deaminase to accept DNA adenine is a genuine chemical step and should be named in the citation. I still do not follow you to a Liu, Komor and Gaudelli prize, because that spends all three seats on one part and leaves no room for a second achievement, and I would need the Target-AID priority record before I treat the trio as uncontested.

responses.point: A prize pairing base editing with PROTAC degradation gives two achievements each explainable in a sentence, with large generative potential, using the three-person limit on the two best-supported entries.
responses.response: The pairing is coherent and I take the generative-potential argument seriously. My difficulty is with B009. No PROTAC is an approved drug, the 2001 concept rests on a peptide-based, cell-impermeable first generation, and the credit splits between the heterobifunctional lineage and the cereblon glue lineage. As someone who asks whether the mechanism was actually established structurally, I find the ternary-complex evidence maturing but not yet settled for a citation. I keep B009 as an alternative, and I would sooner take a mature achievement with clean attribution for the second seat. I agree with your point that a Liu-only credit costs Komor and Gaudelli, and I would put the evolved deaminase and the editor architecture in the citation text.

responses.point: A two-achievement prize can pair a classical synthetic method with a genome-engineering tool, but it may read as a prize without a unifying theme; B003 is mature and cleanly attributed.
responses.response: I agree that a unifying theme is not required for a two-part chemistry prize, and I share your preference for clean attribution, which is why I keep B025. On B003 I differ: the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Kosugi precursor make C-N coupling look more incremental to me than a new architecture does. I also do not accept your point that the dye-sensitized cell's lasting contribution is only the dyes. The mesoporous oxide film with a sensitizer and a mediator is the architecture, and perovskite cells inherited it, so that part is not superseded in the way a single device record would be.

responses.point: A Liu-only credit for base editing is defensible because he is the intellectual originator, and Nishida and Kondo have a real Target-AID precedent that must be handled.
responses.response: I agree Liu is the originator and that Komor and Gaudelli are excluded by the cap, not by judgement. I also share your concern on Target-AID: the Nishida and Kondo fusion appeared at about the same time, and I cannot settle priority from the shortlist. My view is that it changes the citation wording, which should name the programmable conversion of bases without double-strand cleavage and not a particular editor, more than it changes the laureates. If the record shows genuine independent priority, I would revisit the name list. On B060 you suggested recognising dye cells first respects the chronology, and I agree, though I would not hold perovskites back from a later year.

uncertainties: Whether Liu alone is defensible for B024, and whether the Kondo and Nishida priority record changes the credited names, not just the wording.
Whether two names for B025 is the correct cut: I have not verified relative credit for Grätzel, O'Regan and Hagfeldt from the primary papers.
Whether the committee will see the dye-sensitized cell as a completed achievement or as superseded by perovskites, and whether B060 should instead be recognised in a later year.
Whether pairing a materials achievement with a genome-chemistry achievement is acceptable, or whether the committee prefers B024 alone or with B009.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Peter Brzezinski, who ranked B038 first in round 1 and now supports B024 and B009. My own work in porous and framework materials is near but not part of any shortlisted candidate, and none of the credited names for B025 or B024 is a known collaborator or mentor. No change from round 1.
